content: MYLK2, also referred to as myosin light chain kinase 2, is an enzyme encoded by the MYLK2 gene in humans. This enzyme is a calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase that is specifically expressed in adult skeletal muscle tissue. The MYLK2 gene predominantly expresses skMLCK (skeletal muscle myosin light chain kinase) in fast-twitch muscle fibers compared to slow-twitch muscle fibers. Calmodulin, a calcium-binding messenger protein, consists of two terminal domains (N-terminal and C-terminal), each containing two EF-hand motifs that bind calcium ions (Ca²⁺). When calmodulin becomes saturated with Ca²⁺, it undergoes a conformational change, enabling it to interact with target proteins such as skMLCK. This interaction enhances the affinity of calmodulin for Ca²⁺, ultimately facilitating sustained muscle contraction. An illustrative image of a similar complex (sdCen/skMLCK2) is often used to depict this interaction under the context of myosin light chain kinase. The binding of calmodulin to skMLCK plays a critical role in maintaining prolonged muscle activity. Clinically, mutations in the MYLK2 gene have been associated with midventricular hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a condition characterized by abnormal thickening of the heart's midventricular walls.
